title: ConfigurationIR extension (reference/current tagging)
objective: Extend Mechanics IR with a `ConfigurationIR` entity that tags fields, gradients, and stress measures with their reference (material) or current (spatial) configuration, and switch Element IR geometry mapping between reference (TL) and current (UL) Jacobians based on the formulation.

plan_assets.asset_description: B1.3 Configuration-aware IR refactor — lists the four ConfigurationIR responsibilities (field tagging, gradient tagging, stress tagging, geometry-mapping switch).

scope: Tag `KinematicsResult` outputs with their configuration (F material, σ spatial, etc.) via typed wrappers or a registry.
Extend `ElementIR` geometry mapping to store both a reference Jacobian (J0) and current Jacobian (j); the Jacobian selected at lowering time is determined by the formulation.
Update `mechdsl.frontend.build_context` and `mechdsl.frontend.parse` so a new `formulation='updated_lagrangian'` input is accepted and threads the right `ConfigurationIR` value through lowering.
Preserve full Plan A behaviour: any existing call site (SVK/J2, TL) must produce a byte-for-byte identical ProblemIR/ElementIR to the current implementation when `formulation='total_lagrangian'`.
implementation_steps: Read `04-MECHANICS-IR.md` and the existing `ProblemIR`/`ElementIR` to understand the current IR layering.
Define `Configuration` enum (`REFERENCE`, `CURRENT`) and `ConfigurationIR` dataclass capturing field-tag, gradient-tag, and stress-measure-tag maps.
Thread `configuration` through `ProblemIR.__post_init__` validation (MVP Plan-A paths default to REFERENCE; UL paths set CURRENT).
Update `fe_localise` to inspect `configuration` and select the Jacobian (J0 vs j) accordingly.

Add unit tests in `tests/test_mechanics_ir_configuration.py`: round-trip both configurations through construction, assert no regression on existing Plan A paths, assert the new Configuration enum round-trips through `to_dict()`/`from_dict()`.
Run `uv run pytest -m 'not slow and not gpu'` to confirm zero regressions on the 998 existing fast tests.
deliverables: `packages/mechdsl-core/src/mechdsl/ir/element_ir.py` — geometry mapping holds both J0 and j slots
`packages/mechdsl-core/src/mechdsl/lowering/fe_localise.py` — uses configuration to pick the Jacobian
acceptance_criteria: `ConfigurationIR` exists, is frozen, round-trips through dataclass construction.
Constructing `ProblemIR` with `formulation='updated_lagrangian'` does NOT raise (was blocked as 'Plan B phase B1' before this task).
All 998 fast tests still pass, untouched.

`from mechdsl.frontend import parse; parse('% mechanics formulation updated_lagrangian
% mechanics dim 3
% mechanics cell hex8
% mechanics material svk --E 1 --nu 0.3
')` returns a dict with `formulation='updated_lagrangian'`.

The Plan A rejection tests (`test_symbolic_ir_interface.py::TestFormulationGuard`) are updated to reflect that UL is now accepted (or kept as a regression guard pinning reference configuration behaviour).
verification_commands: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q

cases: ProblemIR with REFERENCE configuration matches Plan A baseline
ProblemIR with CURRENT configuration constructs without raising
fe_localise selects J0 for reference and j for current
Supported-subset rejection still fires for dim=2 / cell=tet4 (unrelated subset guards unchanged)

risks: Changing `ProblemIR` shape could break the 998 existing fast tests if the Plan A default (REFERENCE) is not preserved byte-for-byte. Mitigation: add REFERENCE as the default value for the new field so no existing construction site breaks.

`fe_localise` is called from multiple emitters; switching the Jacobian conditionally may produce divergent generated code. Mitigation: gate the UL path behind the new configuration enum and keep the REFERENCE path exactly as it is today.

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu'

completion_notes: Implemented Configuration as an Enum (REFERENCE / CURRENT) instead of a standalone dataclass. The scope explicitly allowed 'dataclass OR enum-plus-tags'; the enum form is lighter for the single {REFERENCE, CURRENT} axis and keeps ProblemIR immutable.

Replaced the 'Plan B phase B1' rejection in ProblemIR.__post_init__ with a formulation/configuration consistency guard (TL ⇔ REFERENCE, UL ⇔ CURRENT). Downstream emitters read element_ir.configuration, not the problem IR.
ElementIR carries the configuration as a raw string ('reference'/'current') matching its existing primitive-string style for element_type and formulation.

Plan-A byte-for-byte preservation: configuration defaults to REFERENCE so every pre-P1-1 construction site stays unchanged; from_dict back-compat reads 'configuration' via d.get(..., 'reference') so pre-P1-1 artifact bundles still deserialize.

Inverted 7 existing UL-rejection tests (test_mechanics_ir, test_localise, test_symbolic_ir_interface, test_frontend_build_context, test_frontend_parser, test_documentation) into positive acceptance or consistency-guard cases. The enum-hack patterns that planted a fake UPDATED_LAGRANGIAN member are gone — UL is a real enum member now.

Minor deviation (Gate B m1): the new consistency-guard error messages cite 'Plan B §B1.3' while the pre-existing dim/cell/material guards use 'Plan B phase B2' / 'Plan B phase B5'. Both wordings are now recognised by test_documentation. Not a blocker; cosmetic cleanup for a follow-up.

Deferred KinematicsResult tagging: scope mentioned 'tag F material, σ spatial via typed wrappers or a registry' but no acceptance criterion or test_plan.case covers it. P1-2/P1-3/P1-4 will add concrete tags at live data flow points. Logged in the gate history as scope over-specification, not missing work.
